title: Safety of the Medical Adaptive Compression System circaid® juxtalite® in patients with CVI (C3-C6) and additionally existing diabetic foot syndrome and PAD
summary:
You are an in-patient at the Clinic for Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. According to the guidelines, compression therapy is to be used for the chronic venous insufficiency (weak veins) with edema (water retention) in the lower legs from which you suffer. Since you also suffer from diabetic foot syndrome and peripheral vascular disease (intermittent claudication), it is unclear whether compression therapy is safe based on current knowledge. 
In this study, we want to examine the safety of the medical adaptive compression system Circaid juxtalite from the company medi within the scope of its approval.

interventions.name: Application of the medical adaptive compression system circaid® juxtalite® to one leg for three consecutive days in ascending pressure ranges (20-30, 30-40, 40-50mmHg), the day before the first application serves as a control day without application of the test product

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Chronic venous insufficiency (CEAP C3-C6) with existing edema on the lower leg on the leg included in the study
- Diabetes mellitus (at least 2 years and at least one medication) with DFS on the leg included in the study
- Evidence of atherosclerosis in the arteries of the leg included in the study
- ABI ≥ 0.5 on the leg included in the study, pole test if ABI >1.3 (suspected medial sclerosis)
- Patient must be able to be mobilized to the edge of the bed for the measurements and remain there for 15 minutes
Exclusion criteria:
- Decompensated heart failure (NYHA III-IV)
- Ankle arterial pressure < 50 mmHg on the leg included in the study
- Toe pressure < 30 mmHg on the leg included in the study
- TcPo2 < 20 mmHg on the arch of the foot on the leg included in the study
- Daily body temperature (measured in the ear) > 38 °C
- Septic phlebitis
- Phlegmasia coerulea dolens
- Pre-existing critical limb ischemia of the included leg, determined by clinical ischemia diagnostics
- Compression therapy in the 24 h prior to the first measurement
- Crural bypass on the included leg
- Severe cognitive impairment
- Existing pregnancy
